transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

This symptom usually means the motor is running but the drive belt has snapped or slipped off the pulleys. Less commonly, the tensioner pulley (jockey wheel) has failed, or the drum rollers are seized. To narrow this down safely: please unplug the dryer and try turning the drum by hand. Does it spin freely with no resistance at all (suggesting a broken belt), does it feel stiff or stuck (suggesting an obstruction or bad bearings), or is there some normal friction?
ive unplugged it and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy almost no resistance

The fact that the drum spins freely by hand suggests the motor is running but the drive belt has either snapped or slipped off its pulleys. This is a very common failure on Hotpoint dryers and explains why the clothes aren't turning. You can order these parts using your model number from an appliance spares retailer; they are generally straightforward to fit once you remove the top or rear panel of the dryer.

candidates: Drive belt has snapped or slipped off (high)
Jockey/idler pulley failed (no tension on belt) (medium)
Motor capacitor weak or seized drum rollers (low)
